name: How do you maintain enough storage after removing upper kitchen cabinets?

mainEntity.name: How do you maintain enough storage after removing upper kitchen cabinets?

acceptedAnswer.text: Losing a wall usually means losing upper cabinets, so compensating for lost storage requires intentional planning. The most common solution is installing an expanded kitchen island with deep drawers, under-counter shelving, and back-to-back cabinetry. Many homeowners also opt for full-height pantry cabinets running floor-to-ceiling along remaining perimeter walls, built-in dining banquettes with storage, or converting an adjacent closet into a dedicated walk-in pantry to offset the eliminated upper cabinets.
acceptedAnswer.description: You can recover storage by installing a multi-functional kitchen island, tall pantry cabinets, ceiling-height perimeter storage, or dedicated walk-in pantries.
